newsitem.title: PERU: Peru MRTA negotiator is experienced revolutionary.
newsitem.headline: Peru MRTA negotiator is experienced revolutionary.

text.p: Rolly Rojas, Marxist rebels' negotiator in talks with the Peruvian government that start Tuesday, is a transport worker-turned-revolutionary who rose to prominence in the group after tunneling out of jail.
The 34-year-old Rojas, known by his nom de guerre "The Arab", came from a poor family and spent his youth working as a busfare collector in Lima, according to anti-terrorism police.
In 1980, he began studying sociology at Lima's San Martin de Porres University where he also became involved with the Cuban-inspired Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).

His armed activities began in 1985 when he participated in assaults on a police headquarters and a bank in the same San Isidro district of Lima where he and about 14 other MRTA members are now holding 72 VIP hostages.
Rojas also took part, according to the police, in bombings of two restaurants and a shopping centre before his arrest in July 1986 while trying to steal a car.
He was sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment in 1989 but escaped the following year with 46 other MRTA members after building a tunnel from the maximum security Castro Castro jail in Lima.

Rojas then left Lima to join the rebel activities in the eastern jungle zone where he rose in the ranks of the MRTA and trained for his role in the storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence last Dec. 17.
Rojas is number two to MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, who led the siege.

Photographers who entered the diplomatic residence to interview the MRTA rebels said the stockily-built, dark-haired Rojas had his face covered with a bandana, clutched an automatic rifle and wore a ribbon round his arm.
Former hostages describe Rojas as intelligent, affable and open to dialogue, while President Alberto Fujimori said in London that his anticipated presence was an encouraging element to the talks.
